disclaimer: Always confirm requirements with your vet and the official authority before travel.

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Your pet must be microchipped before the rabies vaccination is given. The chip must be readable by an ISO 11785 scanner. If it cannot be read on arrival, the pet may be quarantined or refused entry.

source.title: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: Pet Travel Portal

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: The rabies vaccine must be given after the microchip, when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, by an authorised vet. After a primary vaccination you must wait at least 21 days before entering Ireland (longer if the vaccine datasheet says so). Boosters given without a break in cover have no waiting period.

source.title: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: Pet Travel Portal

rules.title: Pet passport or EU Animal Health Certificate
rules.explanation: Your pet needs a valid EU pet passport (owner resident in the EU) or an EU Animal Health Certificate (owner not resident in the EU), endorsed by an official vet within 10 days of arrival. Carry originals, not copies.

source.title: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: Pet Travel Portal

rules.title: Tapeworm treatment (dogs)
rules.explanation: A vet must treat your dog for tapeworm (Echinococcus multilocularis) with a product containing praziquantel, no less than 24 hours and no more than 120 hours before the dog's scheduled arrival time in Ireland, and record it in the pet passport or health certificate. Needed before every entry.

exemptions.description: Not needed for dogs arriving from Finland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland.

source.title: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: Pet Travel Portal

rules.title: Rabies antibody blood test
rules.explanation: From countries not on Ireland's lists, your pet needs a rabies blood (titre) test: sample taken at least 30 days after vaccination, tested at an EU-approved laboratory, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. The pet must then wait 3 months from the date of the blood draw before entering. The wait does not apply if the sample was taken in the EU (or a listed European territory) and recorded in the passport before the pet left, with no break in rabies cover.

exemptions.description: No 3-month wait if the blood sample was taken in the EU or a listed European territory before leaving, and rabies cover was never broken.

source.title: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: Pet Travel Portal

rules.title: Advance notice and compliance check
rules.explanation: Arriving from a non-EU country, you must give advance notice through the DAFM Advance Notice Portal and book a compliance check on arrival. Do not leave the port or airport before the check.

source.title: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: Pet Travel Portal

rules.title: Approved points of entry
rules.explanation: Pets may only enter Ireland through Cork Airport, Dublin Airport, Dublin Port, Shannon Airport, the Port of Cork at Ringaskiddy or Rosslare Europort.

source.title: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: Pet Travel Portal

rules.title: Maximum of 5 pets
rules.explanation: More than 5 pets cannot travel under the non-commercial pet rules (except for a show or competition, with written confirmation). Above 5, the commercial movement rules apply.

source.title: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine: Pet Travel Portal

rules.title: XL Bully import ban
rules.explanation: Importing XL Bully type dogs into Ireland has been prohibited since 1 October 2024.

source.title: gov.ie: Ban on XL Bully dogs

rules.verificationNote: Taken from a search extract of the gov.ie page; the page itself has not been read directly.

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Your pet must be identified by a microchip. The rabies vaccination must not be dated before the microchip.

source.title: European Commission: Travelling with a pet within the EU

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: The pet must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated, the vaccination must not be dated before the microchip, and it only becomes valid 21 days after the primary vaccination. Later vaccinations must be given within the validity of the previous one.

source.title: European Commission: Travelling with a pet within the EU

rules.title: EU pet passport
rules.explanation: Your pet must travel with a passport issued by an authorised vet, recording the microchip and rabies vaccination details.

source.title: European Commission: Travelling with a pet within the EU

rules.title: Maximum of 5 pets
rules.explanation: No more than 5 pets may be moved non-commercially (5 in a single vehicle), unless travelling to a competition, show or sporting event with written evidence and the animals are over 6 months old.

source.title: European Commission: Travelling with a pet within the EU

rules.title: Tapeworm treatment (dogs)
rules.explanation: Dogs entering Finland, Malta or Norway must be treated by a vet with praziquantel (or equivalent) not more than 120 hours and not less than 24 hours before the scheduled entry, certified in the passport.

exemptions.description: Not needed for dogs moving directly between Finland, Ireland, Malta, Northern Ireland and Norway.

source.title: European Commission: Movement of pets

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Your pet must be microchipped before, or at the same time as, its rabies vaccination.

source.title: GOV.UK: Bringing your pet dog, cat or ferret to Great Britain

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: Your pet must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated. You must wait at least 21 full days after the first vaccination before entering Great Britain (day 1 is the day after vaccination).

source.title: GOV.UK: Rabies vaccination and boosters

rules.title: Pet travel document
rules.explanation: Coming from an EU country, your pet needs a pet passport issued in an EU country (or certain other countries), or a Great Britain pet health certificate.

source.title: GOV.UK: Which pet travel document

rules.title: Tapeworm treatment (dogs)
rules.explanation: A vet must treat your dog for tapeworm no less than 24 hours and no more than 120 hours (5 days) before you enter Great Britain, and record the product, date and time in the passport or certificate.

exemptions.description: Not needed for dogs coming directly from Finland, Ireland, Northern Ireland, Malta or Norway.

source.title: GOV.UK: Tapeworm treatment for dogs

rules.title: Banned dog types
rules.explanation: You cannot bring a banned type of dog into Great Britain unless it already has a valid Certificate of Exemption. Banned types: Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, XL Bully. Whether a dog is a banned type depends on what it looks like, not its breed name.

source.title: GOV.UK: Banned dogs

rules.title: More than 5 pets
rules.explanation: Extra rules apply if you bring more than 5 pets, unless you are attending a competition, show or sporting event.

source.title: GOV.UK: Bringing your pet dog, cat or ferret to Great Britain

rules.title: Great Britain pet health certificate
rules.explanation: From countries that do not issue an accepted pet passport, your pet needs a Great Britain pet health certificate, signed, stamped and dated by an official veterinarian. You must enter Great Britain within 10 days of the certificate being issued.

source.title: GOV.UK: Great Britain pet health certificate

rules.title: Rabies blood test (unlisted countries)
rules.explanation: From a country that is not listed, your pet needs a blood sample taken at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, tested at an EU-approved laboratory, showing at least 0.5 IU/ml. You must then wait 3 months from the date the sample was taken before you travel. The wait does not apply if the pet was vaccinated, blood tested and given its passport or certificate in the EU before going to the unlisted country.

exemptions.description: No 3-month wait if the blood test was done in the EU before leaving.

source.title: GOV.UK: Rabies blood tests

rules.title: Approved routes
rules.explanation: You can only use certain travel routes and companies to enter Great Britain, and on a plane pets must usually travel as cargo. You do not need an approved route when travelling within the UK or from Ireland.

source.title: GOV.UK: Travel routes for pets

rules.title: From Northern Ireland
rules.explanation: From Northern Ireland your pet does not need a pet passport or health certificate to enter Great Britain, but it must be microchipped.

source.title: GOV.UK: Which pet travel document

rules.title: Country not approved by Australia
rules.explanation: Cats and dogs can only be imported to Australia from approved countries. From any other country, the pet must first move to an approved country and complete every import step there.

source.title: DAFF: Step-by-step guides to bring your cat or dog to Australia

rules.title: Dog breeds not allowed into Australia
rules.explanation: Pure breeds banned from Australia: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, American Pit Bull Terrier or Pit Bull Terrier, Perro de Presa Canario. Wolfdog hybrids (Czechoslovakian, Saarloos, Lupo Italiano, Kunming) and their crosses are also not allowed. Mixed-breed dogs are allowed if they meet all other conditions.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Cat breeds not allowed into Australia
rules.explanation: Non-domestic cat hybrids such as Savannah cats are not allowed into Australia. As of 1 March 2026, Bengal cats are no longer permitted to enter.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your cat to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Your pet must have a working microchip readable by an ISO compatible reader before the import process starts. It is scanned at every vet visit and must match every document. Numbers starting 999 are not accepted.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Import permit
rules.explanation: Apply for an import permit through BICON and pay in full. Most permits are issued in 20 to 40 business days; it can take up to 123. The permit is valid for up to 12 months and must be valid on the date of export.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.verificationNote: Read in browser 2026-11-26: the cited Group 3 dog guide says the permit is valid until the rabies test (RNATT) expires, 12 months from the blood sample, and must be valid on the date the dog arrives in Australia. 'Valid for up to 12 months' and 'valid at the time of export' are the Group 2 dog guide's wording. Human look: split the rule per group or reword.

rules.title: Book post-entry quarantine
rules.explanation: After the permit is issued, book the Mickleham post-entry quarantine facility. All quarantine costs must be paid before release.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Arrival in Melbourne and quarantine
rules.explanation: Pets must arrive directly into Melbourne International Airport; domestic transfers are not permitted. They stay at least 10 days at the Mickleham quarantine facility. From Group 3 countries the stay is 30 days unless identity was verified before the rabies blood test.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Not eligible if pregnant or nursing
rules.explanation: At export the pet must not be under quarantine restrictions, more than 30 days pregnant, or nursing.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Identity check by the government vet
rules.explanation: An official government veterinarian in the export country must verify the pet's identity and send the declaration directly to DAFF. The pet is eligible for import 180 days after this check. Pet passports and vaccination cards are not accepted instead.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 2 country

rules.verificationNote: Read from the dog guide; the Group 2 cat guide was not read separately.

rules.title: Pre-export checks on the permit
rules.explanation: Complete every health check, treatment and vaccination listed on the import permit with a government approved vet, then a final vet check and health certificate before export.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 2 country

rules.verificationNote: The detailed timings for Group 2 are on the permit and in the guide's later steps, which were not read in full.

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: The vaccine must be given when the pet is at least 84 days old, be approved in the export country, and stay valid continuously from the blood test until the date of export. If it lapses, the pet must be vaccinated and tested again and the 180 days restart.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Identity check before the blood test (optional)
rules.explanation: Optional, but it cuts quarantine from at least 30 days to at least 10. An official government vet verifies the pet's identity at least 180 days before export and before blood is taken for the rabies test. It cannot be done at the same visit as the blood test.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Rabies antibody test (RNATT)
rules.explanation: A government approved vet takes blood after vaccination (3 to 4 weeks after a first vaccination) for a FAVN or RFFIT test; the result must be 0.5 IU/ml or more. The pet cannot be exported for at least 180 days after the sample arrives at the laboratory, and the test is valid for 12 months from sampling. PawRoute counts from the sampling date, so allow extra days for the sample to reach the lab.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: RNATT declaration
rules.explanation: An official government veterinarian completes, signs and stamps the country-specific RNATT declaration from the vaccination certificate and laboratory report. You need it to apply for the import permit.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Leptospirosis: vaccination or test (dogs)
rules.explanation: Dogs must either be fully vaccinated against Leptospira interrogans serovar Canicola, with the booster or final primary dose given between 12 months and 14 days before export, or test negative (MAT) within 45 days of export.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Leishmania test (dogs)
rules.explanation: A government approved vet takes blood for a Leishmania infantum test (IFAT or ELISA; rapid tests are not accepted) within 45 days of export. The result must be negative.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Brucella canis test (dogs that are not desexed)
rules.explanation: Only for dogs that are not desexed: a blood test for Brucella canis (RSAT, TAT or IFAT) within 45 days of export, with a negative result.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Canine influenza vaccination (dogs from the USA, South Korea and Canada)
rules.explanation: Dogs from the USA and South Korea must be fully vaccinated against canine influenza: primary course finished at least 14 days before export, or a booster between 12 months and 14 days before export. Dogs from Canada may instead be isolated for 10 days and test negative within 7 days of export.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: External parasite treatment (dogs)
rules.explanation: A government approved vet treats the dog with a product that kills ticks and fleas on contact, starting at least 30 days before export and repeated as the manufacturer directs until export.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: External parasite treatment (cats)
rules.explanation: A government approved vet treats the cat for ticks and fleas, starting at least 21 days before export and repeated as the manufacturer directs until export.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your cat to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Internal parasite treatment, first dose
rules.explanation: The pet must be treated for nematodes and cestodes twice within 45 days before export, at least 14 days apart. This is the first treatment.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Internal parasite treatment, second dose
rules.explanation: The second internal parasite treatment must be given within 5 days before export, at least 14 days after the first. It can be done at the final vet check.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Pre-export clinical exam and health certificate
rules.explanation: Within 5 days before export, a government approved vet examines the pet and completes the veterinary health certificate, which an official government vet then endorses. Bring the permit and all laboratory reports.

source.title: DAFF: How to bring your dog to Australia from a Group 3 country

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: The pet must be identified with an ISO 11784/11785 microchip (15-digit numeric) before the first rabies vaccination. Numbers starting 900 202 are not accepted.

source.title: MAFF Animal Quarantine Service: Import of dogs and cats from non-designated regions

rules.title: Two rabies vaccinations
rules.explanation: After microchipping, the pet needs rabies vaccination twice or more. The first when at least 91 days old (birth is day 0); the second 30 days or more after the first and within the first vaccine's effective period. Only inactivated or recombinant vaccines are accepted.

source.title: MAFF Animal Quarantine Service: Import of dogs and cats from non-designated regions

rules.title: Rabies antibody test and 180-day wait
rules.explanation: After the second vaccination, blood is tested at a laboratory designated by Japan; the result must be 0.5 IU/ml or more. The pet must then wait 180 days from the sampling date (day 0) before arriving, and arrive within 2 years of sampling. A shorter wait means detention at quarantine for the shortfall.

source.title: MAFF Animal Quarantine Service: Import of dogs and cats from non-designated regions

rules.title: Advance notification to Animal Quarantine Service
rules.explanation: Notify the Animal Quarantine Service office for your port of arrival not less than 40 days before arrival in Japan, through NACCS or by e-mail form. Later notices are in principle not accepted.

source.title: MAFF Animal Quarantine Service: Import of dogs and cats from non-designated regions

rules.title: Clinical inspection before departure
rules.explanation: A vet must inspect the pet within 10 days before boarding and find no clinical signs of rabies (and, for dogs, leptospirosis).

source.title: MAFF Animal Quarantine Service: Import of dogs and cats from non-designated regions

rules.title: Government-endorsed certificate (Form AC)
rules.explanation: Get the certificate (Form AC recommended) completed by your vet and endorsed by the government agency of the exporting country, covering microchip, vaccinations, antibody test and clinical inspection. Originals are required.

source.title: MAFF Animal Quarantine Service: Import of dogs and cats from non-designated regions

rules.title: Residency in a rabies-free designated region
rules.explanation: From a designated region (Iceland, Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, Hawaii, Guam) the pet must have lived there since birth, for at least 180 days immediately before export, or since being imported directly from Japan. Otherwise it is detained for the shortfall. The certificate (Form AB) must be endorsed by the exporting government.

source.title: MAFF Animal Quarantine Service: Import of dogs and cats from designated regions

rules.title: Ports of entry for dogs
rules.explanation: Dogs can be imported only through 19 ports. Airports: New Chitose, Narita, Haneda, Chubu, Kansai, Itami, Kobe, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka, Kagoshima, Naha. For cats arriving elsewhere, contact Animal Quarantine Service in advance.

source.title: MAFF Animal Quarantine Service: Import of dogs and cats from non-designated regions

rules.title: Check you qualify under the baggage rule
rules.explanation: Pets (up to 2 dogs or cats) can be brought as baggage only by owners transferring residence to India after two years abroad, with proof of both. For short visits and anything else, a DGFT licence is needed first. Importing dogs for breeding or commercial purposes is not permitted.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): Import of pets under baggage

rules.title: Maximum of 2 pets
rules.explanation: The baggage rule covers up to 2 dogs or cats per owner.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): Import of pets under baggage

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: Dogs three months of age and older must be vaccinated against rabies more than one month, but within 12 months, before actual embarkation. The record must be officially certified.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): Import of pets under baggage

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: Cats must be vaccinated against rabies more than one month, but within 12 months, before actual embarkation. The record must be officially certified.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): Import of pets under baggage

rules.title: Other vaccinations (dogs)
rules.explanation: The official health certificate must certify the dog free from clinical signs of rabies, canine distemper, parvovirus infection and leptospirosis, with all other vaccination records officially certified.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): Import of pets under baggage

rules.title: Other vaccinations (cats)
rules.explanation: The official health certificate must certify the cat free from clinical signs of rabies, distemper, feline enteritis, feline panleukopenia and leptospirosis, with vaccination records officially certified.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): Import of pets under baggage

rules.title: Official health certificate
rules.explanation: Get the official health certificate from the country of origin. The owner's name must match the ticket, and it must carry the owner's addresses in both countries. AQCS keeps the original on arrival.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): Import of pets under baggage

rules.title: Advance NOC from AQCS
rules.explanation: Apply to the Animal Quarantine station at your port of entry for an advance No Objection Certificate. It can be issued within 7 days before arrival from self-certified copies of the documents. Without it the airline will not board the pet. Fee Rs.1000 per application.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): Import of pets under baggage

rules.title: Ports of entry
rules.explanation: Pets can enter India only through New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bangalore or Hyderabad, where they are examined at the Quarantine Station. In case of doubt a pet may be kept under quarantine observation, with final clearance after 30 days.

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): FAQ

rules.title: Proof of age (under 3 months)
rules.explanation: For a puppy or kitten under 3 months travelling with its owner, bring proof of the animal's age from a veterinarian. No rabies certificate is needed at this age.

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

rules.title: Rabies vaccination certificate (dogs 8 months or older)
rules.explanation: A personal pet dog 8 months or older needs a valid rabies vaccination certificate, and must appear healthy. Dogs must have been at least 3 months old when vaccinated. Canada sets no waiting period after vaccination. The certificate must be in English or French, signed by a licensed vet, identify the animal, and give the vaccination date, vaccine trade name and serial number, and period of validity. An EU pet passport with these details is accepted.

requirement.ifNotMet: If this is not met, CFIA requires the owner to have the animal vaccinated within a set period at their own expense and show the record to a CFIA office.

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

rules.title: Rabies certificate or Rabies Country-Freedom Certificate (dogs 8 months or older)
rules.explanation: From a country Canada recognises as rabies-free, a dog 8 months or older needs either a valid rabies vaccination certificate or a Rabies Country-Freedom Certificate from the government veterinary authority, stating the dog has been in that country since birth or for at least 6 months. The certificate must be in English or French, signed by a licensed vet, identify the animal, and give the vaccination date, vaccine trade name and serial number, and period of validity. An EU pet passport with these details is accepted.

requirement.ifNotMet: A Rabies Country-Freedom Certificate is accepted instead. If this is not met, CFIA requires the owner to have the animal vaccinated within a set period at their own expense and show the record to a CFIA office.

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

rules.title: Rabies vaccination certificate (dogs 3 to 8 months)
rules.explanation: A personal pet dog between 3 and 8 months needs a valid rabies vaccination certificate. Extra conditions apply at this age, depending on whether the dog travels with its owner.

requirement.ifNotMet: If this is not met, CFIA requires the owner to have the animal vaccinated within a set period at their own expense and show the record to a CFIA office.

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

rules.verificationNote: The CFIA answer for dogs aged 3 to 8 months is longer than the one read; only its first requirement is captured.

rules.title: Rabies vaccination certificate (cats 3 months or older)
rules.explanation: A domestic cat 3 months or older needs a valid rabies vaccination certificate. The certificate must be in English or French, signed by a licensed vet, identify the animal, and give the vaccination date, vaccine trade name and serial number, and period of validity. An EU pet passport with these details is accepted.

requirement.ifNotMet: If this is not met, CFIA requires the owner to have the animal vaccinated within a set period at their own expense and show the record to a CFIA office.

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

rules.title: Rabies certificate (cats from rabies-free countries)
rules.explanation: A domestic cat 3 months or older needs a valid rabies vaccination certificate; from a country Canada recognises as rabies-free a different CFIA answer applies.

requirement.ifNotMet: If this is not met, CFIA requires the owner to have the animal vaccinated within a set period at their own expense and show the record to a CFIA office.

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

rules.verificationNote: The CFIA answer for cats from rabies-free countries was not read; the general cat rule is shown.

rules.title: Microchip not required
rules.explanation: Canada does not require a microchip or tattoo for domestic dogs imported as personal pets or for domestic cats. Provinces and municipalities set their own rules on which animals may be kept.

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

rules.title: Import permit for ferrets
rules.explanation: A ferret 3 months or older from a country other than the United States needs a CFIA import permit, applied for at least 30 days before travel. Contact the provincial authority for permission to keep ferrets.

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

rules.title: Dogs must be at least 6 months old
rules.explanation: Dogs must be at least 6 months old at the time of entry to the United States.

source.title: CDC: Dogs from dog rabies-free or low-risk countries

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Dogs must have a microchip that can be detected with a universal scanner.

source.title: CDC: Dogs from dog rabies-free or low-risk countries

rules.title: CDC Dog Import Form
rules.explanation: A free CDC Dog Import Form is required for each dog; you get a receipt by email. From rabies-free or low-risk countries this is the only document required, the receipt is valid for 6 months and multiple entries, and the dog can enter at any airport, seaport or land crossing. Dogs under one year need a photo taken within 15 days before travel.

source.title: CDC: Dogs from dog rabies-free or low-risk countries

rules.verificationNote: Read 2026-11-25: the cited CDC low-risk page does not state the photo rule for dogs under one year (that sentence is on CDC's high-risk page and the form instructions). The rest matches. Needs a human look: cite the form instructions page or drop the sentence.

rules.title: Where your dog has been in the last 6 months
rules.explanation: The United States looks at every country the dog has been in during the 6 months before entry, not only the country you fly from. If that includes a country CDC lists as high-risk for dog rabies, the high-risk rules apply. PawRoute only checks the legs of this trip.

source.title: CDC: Dogs from dog rabies-free or low-risk countries

rules.title: Cats
rules.explanation: Cats are not required to have proof of rabies vaccination to enter the United States, but must appear healthy on arrival. CDC recommends vaccination. Hawaii and Guam apply their own quarantine rules.

source.title: CDC: Bringing an animal into the U.S.

rules.title: Screwworm and foot-and-mouth countries
rules.explanation: USDA has extra rules for dogs coming from countries affected by screwworm (a government vet's certificate after inspection within 5 days before shipment) or foot-and-mouth disease (keep the dog away from livestock for 5 days after entry). Check whether your origin country is listed.

source.title: USDA APHIS: Bring a pet dog into the United States

rules.title: State and territory rules
rules.explanation: Your pet may also need to meet the entry requirements of the US state or territory you are going to. PawRoute holds the rules for some states only. If your state shows no state steps and no state note, contact the state animal health official.

source.title: USDA APHIS: Bring a pet from another country into the United States

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (dogs from high-risk countries)
rules.explanation: For a foreign-vaccinated dog that has been in a high-risk country: microchip first, then a rabies vaccine given at 12 weeks (84 days) of age or older and at least 28 days before the dog enters the United States. Unvaccinated dogs from high-risk countries are not allowed in. Dogs vaccinated in the US follow a different route with a Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination.

source.title: CDC: Foreign-vaccinated dogs from high-risk countries

rules.title: Rabies titer from a CDC-approved laboratory
rules.explanation: A blood sample drawn at least 30 days after the dog's first valid rabies vaccination and at least 28 days before entry, tested at a CDC-approved laboratory. The result stays valid for life if vaccination never lapses.

requirement.ifNotMet: Without a valid titer the dog must have a reservation for a 28-day quarantine at a CDC-registered animal care facility, at your cost.

source.title: CDC: Foreign-vaccinated dogs from high-risk countries

rules.verificationNote: The pass mark is not stated on the CDC page read; 0.5 IU/ml is assumed.

rules.title: Certification of Foreign Rabies Vaccination and Microchip
rules.explanation: This CDC form must be completed no more than 30 days before the dog travels and endorsed by an official government veterinarian of the exporting country. It can be used once and is valid for 30 days after signing.

source.title: CDC: Foreign-vaccinated dogs from high-risk countries

rules.title: Reservation at a CDC-registered animal care facility
rules.explanation: Reserve a CDC-registered animal care facility for examination and revaccination on arrival. The dog must arrive at the airport where that facility is: Atlanta, Dallas Fort Worth, Los Angeles, Miami, New York JFK, Philadelphia, Seattle or Washington Dulles. No onward domestic travel until the facility releases the dog.

source.title: CDC: Approved animal care facilities

rules.verificationNote: Read in browser 2026-11-26: the cited CDC page lists the same eight airports and requires the reservation for exam and revaccination, but does not state 'No onward domestic travel until the facility releases the dog'. Human look: cite the page that says it or drop the sentence.

rules.title: Microchip before the blood test
rules.explanation: The dog or cat must have an electronic microchip implanted before the FAVN rabies blood test. A pet that cannot be identified by scanning is assigned to 120 days quarantine.

source.title: Hawaii Animal Quarantine: Checklist 1, Direct Airport Release and 5 Day Or Less

rules.title: Two rabies vaccinations
rules.explanation: The pet must have been vaccinated against rabies at least twice in its lifetime, more than 30 days apart. The most recent vaccine must be given more than 30 days before arrival in Hawaii and still be within its licensed booster interval. Pets that do not meet every requirement are quarantined for up to 120 days on arrival.

source.title: Hawaii Animal Quarantine: Checklist 1, Direct Airport Release and 5 Day Or Less

rules.title: FAVN rabies antibody test and 30-day wait
rules.explanation: A passing OIE-FAVN test from an approved laboratory (Kansas State, Auburn, Missouri, or the DOD lab), with Hawaii listed as the destination. The pet must wait at least 30 days after a successful test before arriving. The result is valid for 36 months from the day the lab received the blood. PawRoute counts from the sampling date. Pets that do not meet every requirement are quarantined for up to 120 days on arrival.

source.title: Hawaii Animal Quarantine: 5 Day Or Less program FAQ

rules.verificationNote: The pass mark is not stated in the text read; 0.5 IU/ml is assumed.

rules.title: Send the Dog and Cat Import Form (AQS-279)
rules.explanation: The Animal Quarantine Station must receive the AQS-279 form, the two most recent rabies certificates and payment 10 days or more before arrival to qualify for direct airport release at the $185 fee. Later documents mean the $244 fee.

source.title: Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity: Animal Quarantine Information

rules.title: Tick treatment
rules.explanation: Within 14 days before arrival, a vet must treat the pet with a long-acting product labelled to kill ticks (fipronil or equivalent or better) and record it on the health certificate. Revolution is not accepted. Pets found with ticks do not qualify for direct release.

source.title: Hawaii Animal Quarantine: 5 Day Or Less program FAQ

rules.title: Health certificate
rules.explanation: An original health certificate must come with the pet, recording the tick treatment and stating the animal was inspected and found free of New World Screwworm.

source.title: Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity: Animal Quarantine Information

rules.title: Documents from a rabies-free exempt area
rules.explanation: From the British Isles, Australia, Guam or New Zealand: an original health certificate within 14 days of transport from a government veterinarian, an affidavit that the animal was not outside that country in the six months before shipment, and an affidavit that it travelled on one aircraft. From Guam, the Guam affidavit (IC-5).

source.title: Hawaii Animal Quarantine: Checklist for pets from the British Isles, Australia, Guam and New Zealand

rules.title: Is Ireland part of Hawaii's exempt 'British Isles'?
rules.explanation: Hawaii exempts pets from the 'British Isles' from rabies quarantine but does not define the term in the pages read. PawRoute applies the full Hawaii requirements to pets from Ireland and Northern Ireland. Ask the Animal Quarantine Station (rabiesfree@hawaii.gov) whether the exemption covers you.

source.title: Hawaii Animal Quarantine: Checklist for pets from the British Isles, Australia, Guam and New Zealand

rules.title: Arrival airport and inspection hours
rules.explanation: No permit is needed to fly into Honolulu; arrive in time to reach the airport holding facility between 8:00 and 16:30. Flying direct to Kona, Kahului or Lihue needs a Neighbor Island Inspection Permit, with documents received 30 days or more before arrival and a contracted vet.

source.title: Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity: Animal Quarantine Information

rules.title: Ferrets are prohibited in Hawaii
rules.explanation: Ferrets are on Hawaii's list of animals prohibited from entry or possession by private individuals.

source.title: Hawaii Plant Quarantine: Animal guidelines

rules.title: Hybrid cats and dogs are prohibited in Hawaii
rules.explanation: Non-domestic dogs and cats and hybrids such as wolf, wolf cross, Dingo, Bengal and Savannah are prohibited.

source.title: Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity: Animal Quarantine Information

rules.title: Animal entry permit and documents
rules.explanation: Submit the Application for Animal Entry Permit and all import documents at least 30 days before the intended arrival (less than 14 days cannot be guaranteed). Fee $65. Rabies certificates must show the microchip number, and the microchip must have been given before the current rabies vaccination.

source.title: Guam Department of Agriculture: Animal Health and Animal Control

rules.title: Health certificate within 10 days of travel
rules.explanation: A health certificate done within 10 days of travel, showing the microchip number, in English or translated.

source.title: Guam Department of Agriculture: Animal Health and Animal Control

rules.title: FAVN test and 120-day wait (international arrivals)
rules.explanation: International arrivals from non-exempt places do not qualify for home quarantine: the pet must wait the full 120 days after the FAVN sample was received at a CDC-approved lab. Results must be sent straight from the lab. PawRoute counts from the sampling date.

source.title: Guam Department of Agriculture: Animal Health and Animal Control

rules.verificationNote: The pass mark is not stated on the page read; 0.5 IU/ml is assumed.

rules.title: Vet exam within 72 hours of arrival (exempt areas)
rules.explanation: From Australia, the British Isles, Hawaii, Japan or New Zealand: bring the current rabies certificate and either FAVN results or an Affidavit for Export showing 120 days' residence, then take the pet to a private vet on Guam within 72 hours of arrival.

source.title: Guam Department of Agriculture: Animal Health and Animal Control

rules.title: US federal dog rules also apply
rules.explanation: Guam applies the US federal rules for dogs: a CDC Dog Import Form, and all dogs must be at least 6 months old to enter.

source.title: Guam Department of Agriculture: Animal Health and Animal Control

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Your pet must be identified by a microchip. The rabies vaccine must not be dated before the microchip was implanted or read.

source.title: European Commission: Bringing a pet into the EU from a non-EU country

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: The pet must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated, and the vaccination becomes valid not less than 21 days after the primary vaccination is completed.

source.title: European Commission: Bringing a pet into the EU from a non-EU country

rules.title: Rabies antibody test
rules.explanation: From countries not on the EU's lists, a blood sample must be taken at least 30 days after the primary vaccination and tested at a designated laboratory, with a result of 0.5 IU/ml or more. The sample must be taken not less than 90 days before the health certificate is issued. The 90 days do not apply on re-entry if the test was done, with a good result, before the pet left the EU. PawRoute counts the 90 days to arrival, which is slightly generous: the certificate is issued up to 10 days earlier.

exemptions.description: The 90 days do not apply if the test was done in the EU before the pet left.

source.title: European Commission: Bringing a pet into the EU from a non-EU country

rules.title: EU animal health certificate or pet passport
rules.explanation: Your pet needs an animal health certificate issued by an official veterinarian (or endorsed by the competent authority), valid for 10 days from issue for entry and then for up to 6 months of travel within the EU, plus a written owner's declaration. EU residents returning can use a valid EU pet passport instead. An EU pet passport held by a Great Britain resident is no longer valid.

source.title: European Commission: Bringing a pet into the EU from a non-EU country

rules.title: Travellers' point of entry
rules.explanation: Pets from outside the EU must enter through a travellers' point of entry designated by the EU country, where documents and identity are checked.

source.title: European Commission: Bringing a pet into the EU from a non-EU country

rules.title: Maximum of 5 pets
rules.explanation: No more than 5 pets in a single vehicle, unless travelling to a competition, exhibition or sporting event with written evidence and the animals are more than six months old.

source.title: European Commission: Bringing a pet into the EU from a non-EU country

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Entering Switzerland from the EU, pets need a microchip, a valid rabies vaccination and a recognised pet passport.

source.title: Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: The first vaccination is possible from the age of 12 weeks and only becomes valid 21 days later.

source.title: Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: Pet passport
rules.explanation: From the EU, your pet needs an EU or Swiss pet passport.

source.title: Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: Maximum of 5 pets
rules.explanation: A maximum of five pets (dogs, cats and ferrets) can be transported in a single private vehicle.

source.title: Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: Docked ears or tails
rules.explanation: The importation of dogs with docked ears or tails into Switzerland is prohibited.

source.title: Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Your pet must be microchipped before its rabies vaccination. Pets coming from Great Britain under the Northern Ireland Pet Travel Scheme must also be microchipped.

source.title: DAERA: Travelling with pets

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: The pet must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated, and must wait at least 21 days after the primary vaccination (30 if the vaccine datasheet says so).

source.title: DAERA: Travelling with pets

rules.title: Pet passport or Animal Health Certificate
rules.explanation: From EU countries your pet needs an EU pet passport or an Animal Health Certificate (valid 10 days for entry). From other countries it needs an Animal Health Certificate and must enter through a Travellers' Point of Entry.

source.title: DAERA: Travelling with pets

rules.title: Tapeworm treatment (dogs)
rules.explanation: Dogs travelling directly to Northern Ireland must be treated by a vet not more than 120 hours and not less than 24 hours before scheduled entry. It is not required when travelling between Northern Ireland and Ireland.

exemptions.description: Not needed for dogs arriving from Ireland, Finland, Malta or Norway.

source.title: DAERA: Travelling with pets

rules.title: Rabies blood test (unlisted countries)
rules.explanation: From unlisted countries your pet needs a blood test taken at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, at an EU-approved laboratory, and must wait 3 calendar months after the blood test.

source.title: DAERA: Travelling with pets

rules.verificationNote: DAERA points to the EU's lists for which countries are listed; PawRoute uses the lists on the European Commission page.

rules.title: Northern Ireland Pet Travel Document
rules.explanation: Residents of Great Britain need a free Northern Ireland Pet Travel Document to bring a pet directly from Great Britain to Northern Ireland. You apply once and it lasts for as long as you own the pet; no vet visit is needed. Each pet needs its own document and must be microchipped. It cannot be used if you intend to travel onwards to Ireland or another EU country; different requirements apply.

source.title: DAERA: Great Britain to Northern Ireland pet travel guidance

rules.title: Tapeworm treatment from Great Britain
rules.explanation: DAERA's guidance for the Northern Ireland Pet Travel Document does not say whether dogs from Great Britain need tapeworm treatment. Ask DAERA before you travel.

source.title: DAERA: Great Britain to Northern Ireland pet travel guidance

rules.title: Points of entry
rules.explanation: Pets from outside the EU enter through Belfast Port or Larne Port, or by air through Belfast International, Belfast City or City of Derry. For air arrivals, DAERA must be told at least 10 days in advance.

source.title: DAERA: Travelling with pets

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: The animal must be identified by an ISO 11784 microchip before the rabies vaccination. A tattoo is accepted only if done before 3 July 2011.

source.title: Norwegian Food Safety Authority: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets from EU countries to Norway

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: The animal must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated, and the vaccination is valid not less than 21 days after the primary course. A revaccination within validity has no waiting period. No rabies vaccination is required for animals travelling only between Norway and Sweden.

exemptions.description: Not required for animals travelling only between Norway and Sweden.

source.title: Norwegian Food Safety Authority: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets from EU countries to Norway

rules.title: Pet passport
rules.explanation: The animal must travel with a pet passport recording its identification and vaccinations.

source.title: Norwegian Food Safety Authority: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets from EU countries to Norway

rules.title: Maximum of 5 pets
rules.explanation: No more than five dogs, cats or ferrets may accompany the owner during a single non-commercial movement.

source.title: Norwegian Food Safety Authority: Travelling with dogs, cats and ferrets from EU countries to Norway

rules.title: Regular travellers: the 28-day alternative
rules.explanation: Dogs that travel regularly between Norway and EU countries may instead be treated by a vet at least twice at intervals of no more than 28 days before travelling, and then every 28 days for as long as they keep travelling. PawRoute plans the standard 24 to 120 hour treatment.

source.title: Norwegian Food Safety Authority: Mandatory treatment for echinococcosis

rules.title: Minimum age
rules.explanation: A dog or cat must be at least twelve weeks of age at the time of export to Singapore.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.verificationNote: The rule is 12 weeks at export; PawRoute checks 3 months at arrival, which is slightly stricter.

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: Your dog or cat must be microchipped to ISO 11784 or ISO 11785 Annex A, with the number on every vaccination and treatment record.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: From Schedule II and III places, the pet needs a valid rabies vaccination with an inactivated or recombinant vaccine, kept up to date with boosters. Not required from Schedule I places (Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, United Kingdom).

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Rabies serology test
rules.explanation: Blood must be sampled at least 28 days after a valid rabies vaccination, and at least 90 days and within 12 months before the date of export, at a WOAH reference laboratory or an approved laboratory in a Schedule I or II place.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.verificationNote: The pass mark is in the veterinary conditions PDF, which was not read; 0.5 IU/ml is assumed.

rules.title: Dog or cat licence
rules.explanation: Obtain a dog or cat licence on the Pet Animal Licensing System (PALS), and check the breed and number of pets are allowed at your Singapore address.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Import licence
rules.explanation: Apply for and obtain an AVS import licence before arrival. It is valid for 90 days from the date of issue, and must be shown at check-in.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Book the border inspection
rules.explanation: At least 5 days before arrival, book the border control inspection appointment. Arriving without one costs S$133 per hour.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Parasite treatments and health certificate
rules.explanation: Between 2 and 7 days before export, have a vet give external and internal parasite treatments and complete the veterinary health certificate, then have the exporting country's official government vet endorse it.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Quarantine depends on the schedule
rules.explanation: Singapore's quarantine rules depend on the exporting place's schedule and are set out in the veterinary conditions for that schedule. Reserve quarantine space, where needed, once the serology result is ready.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Dog breeds not allowed in Singapore
rules.explanation: Not allowed: Pit Bull types (American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bulldog), Akita, Boerboel, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Neapolitan Mastiff, Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, and crosses of these.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Bengal and Savannah crosses
rules.explanation: First to fourth generation Bengal or Savannah cat crosses are not allowed. Later generations need documentary proof before import.

source.title: Singapore Animal & Veterinary Service: Importing dogs and cats

rules.title: Zoosanitary Import Certificate on arrival
rules.explanation: On arrival, request the Zoosanitary Import Certificate (CZI) at the SENASICA office at your point of entry. Your pet has a physical inspection; ticks must be removed, and the crate must be clean with no bedding, toys or treats.

source.title: SENASICA: Requirements and procedures for traveling to Mexico with your pet

rules.title: Certificate of Good Health
rules.explanation: From countries other than the United States and Canada, bring a Certificate of Good Health (original and a copy) with a maximum validity of 15 days from its date of issue. It must come from an official vet, or a private vet on letterhead with their licence number, and give the exporter's and importer's names and addresses, and state the pet was clinically healthy.

source.title: SENASICA: Requirements and procedures for traveling to Mexico with your pet

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: The health certificate must give the date the rabies vaccine was given and its period of validity. Animals under 3 months of age are exempt.

requirement.ifNotMet: Without a certificate or vaccination record, you must hire a private vet in Mexico to give the treatments and issue the certificate, at your cost.

source.title: SENASICA: Requirements and procedures for traveling to Mexico with your pet

rules.title: Internal and external deworming
rules.explanation: The certificate must state that the pet was dewormed internally and externally within the six months prior to travel and is free of ectoparasites.

source.title: SENASICA: Requirements and procedures for traveling to Mexico with your pet

rules.title: Screwworm inspection document (dogs from the United States)
rules.explanation: Dogs travelling from the United States need a document showing they are free from New World screwworm, signed by a USDA-accredited vet within the 5 days prior to travel. Cats are exempt.

source.title: SENASICA: Requirements and procedures for traveling to Mexico with your pet

rules.title: From the United States or Canada
rules.explanation: From the United States or Canada, a Certificate of Good Health and vaccination record are not needed; the pet has a physical inspection on arrival.

source.title: SENASICA: Requirements and procedures for traveling to Mexico with your pet

rules.title: Country not approved by Iceland
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats can only be imported to Iceland from approved exporting countries. From other countries MAST may authorise import only for a resident of that country who is moving to Iceland and has owned the pet there for at least six months, under the category 2 conditions.

source.title: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST): Import of live animals

rules.title: Six months in an approved country
rules.explanation: The pet must have been in an approved exporting country (or another of the same category) for the last 6 months, or since birth. All dogs and cats count as imports, whatever the length of the visit.

source.title: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST): Import of live animals

rules.title: Import permit
rules.explanation: Apply to MAST for an import permit, with a photo of the pet. The fee is about ISK 40,000 at minimum.

source.title: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST): Import of live animals

rules.title: Book 14 days of quarantine
rules.explanation: Every dog and cat must spend a minimum of 14 days at one of the two quarantine stations (Reykjanesbær or Mósel). They take arrivals on set dates, so book before fixing your flight. Home quarantine is only for certified assistance dogs.

source.title: MAST: Import of live animals, frequently asked questions

rules.title: Microchip
rules.explanation: The pet must have a microchip, and its number must be on every laboratory report. A missing or incorrect microchip is a reason for rejection.

source.title: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST): Import of live animals

rules.title: Rabies vaccination
rules.explanation: Every dog and cat entering Iceland must have a rabies vaccination. Vaccinations given less than 14 days before import are a reason for rejection.

source.title: MAST: Import of live animals, frequently asked questions

rules.title: Rabies antibody test
rules.explanation: A rabies antibody test at an EU-approved laboratory, sampled at least 30 days after a valid rabies vaccination, with a result of at least 0.5 IU/ml. From category 1 countries there is no waiting period once the result is available.

source.title: MAST: Import of live animals, frequently asked questions

rules.title: Rabies antibody test and 90-day wait
rules.explanation: A rabies antibody test at an EU-approved laboratory, sampled at least 30 days after vaccination, with a result of at least 0.5 IU/ml. From category 2 countries at least 90 days must pass from the day the sample was collected before import.

source.title: MAST: Import of live animals, frequently asked questions

rules.title: Leptospirosis and core vaccinations (dogs)
rules.explanation: Dogs need vaccination against leptospirosis, distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus and parainfluenza, with at least 14 days since the last vaccination before entering Iceland.

source.title: MAST: Import of live animals, frequently asked questions

rules.title: Parasite treatment, first
rules.explanation: The pet must have two parasite treatments before import. The first is given 21 to 28 days before. The products are listed in MAST's parasite treatment guide.

source.title: MAST: Import of live animals, frequently asked questions

rules.title: Parasite treatment, second
rules.explanation: The second parasite treatment is given 5 to 10 days before import.

source.title: MAST: Import of live animals, frequently asked questions

rules.title: Send the health certificate to MAST
rules.explanation: The signed health certificate (form D1/D2 for dogs, C1/C2 for cats) must reach MAST no less than 5 days before import, and by 12 noon on the previous Friday. Late paperwork is a reason for rejection.

source.title: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST): Import of live animals

rules.title: Arrival at Keflavík
rules.explanation: All pets must arrive at Keflavík Airport between 06:00 and 17:00. Weekend arrivals are not approved, and arrival by ferry is not permitted.

source.title: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST): Import of live animals

rules.title: Not eligible if pregnant, nursing or recently injured
rules.explanation: Pregnant or lactating animals, and animals injured or recently operated on, may not be imported unless MAST permits.

source.title: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST): Import of live animals

rules.title: Dog breeds not permitted in Iceland
rules.explanation: Not permitted, including crosses for at least 5 generations: Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bulldog, Fila Brasileiro, Tosa Inu, Dogo Argentino, Cane Corso, Presa Canario, Boerboel, and wolf hybrids.

source.title: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST): Import of live animals

rules.title: Special Permit
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats must not be brought into Hong Kong unless a Special Permit is obtained in advance from AFCD. Allow at least 5 working days. The permit is valid for 6 months and one consignment, and lists the conditions your pet must meet.

source.title: Hong Kong AFCD: Import of dogs and cats

rules.title: Quarantine (Group I)
rules.explanation: From Group I places, dogs and cats are normally exempted from quarantine subject to full compliance with the permit conditions.

source.title: Hong Kong AFCD: Import of dogs and cats

rules.title: Quarantine (Group II)
rules.explanation: From Group II places, dogs and cats may be exempted from quarantine subject to full compliance with the permit conditions.

source.title: Hong Kong AFCD: Import of dogs and cats

rules.title: Fighting dogs prohibited
rules.explanation: Fighting dogs under the Dangerous Dogs Regulation are prohibited from import: Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro and their crossbreeds.

source.title: Hong Kong AFCD: Import of dogs and cats

rules.title: Certificate of Veterinary Inspection
rules.explanation: All dogs and cats moving into Alabama need an official Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (electronic or official form; APHIS Form 7001 is not accepted). Certificates are void 30 days after inspection.

source.title: Alabama Department of Agriculture and Industries: Import requirements

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats must be vaccinated against rabies when they reach three months of age. Younger puppies and kittens may be admitted without vaccination.

source.title: Alabama Department of Agriculture and Industries: Import requirements

rules.title: No state certificate for pets staying with their owner
rules.explanation: California's agriculture department has no additional import requirements for cats or dogs that are not changing ownership. A certificate is needed only for dogs changing ownership. Rabies questions go to the public health department.

source.title: California Department of Food and Agriculture: Animal entry requirements

rules.title: Ferrets are a restricted species in California
rules.explanation: Ferrets are on California's restricted-species list. Contact the California Department of Fish and Wildlife before travelling with a ferret.

source.title: California Department of Food and Agriculture: Animal entry requirements

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: A dog or cat entering Florida needs a current rabies vaccination if it is 3 months of age or older.

source.title: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: Dog and cat movement requirements

rules.title: No certificate when travelling with your pet
rules.explanation: Florida requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection issued within 30 days, unless the pet is privately owned and travelling with its owner. Airlines may still ask for one.

source.title: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: Dog and cat movement requirements

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: All dogs and cats entering Georgia must have proof of a current and approved rabies vaccination. Ferrets also need proof of rabies vaccination.

source.title: Georgia Department of Agriculture: Bringing animals into Georgia

rules.title: Ferrets must be neutered
rules.explanation: Ferrets seven months of age or older entering Georgia must be spayed or neutered.

source.title: Georgia Department of Agriculture: Bringing animals into Georgia

rules.title: Certificate of Veterinary Inspection
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats need a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection issued within 30 days of entry, showing age, sex, breed and the full Illinois destination address. From 1 January 2027 it must be electronic.

source.title: Illinois Department of Agriculture: Animal import

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: All dogs and cats 16 weeks of age and older shall be vaccinated against rabies.

source.title: Illinois Department of Agriculture: Animal import

rules.title: Certificate of Veterinary Inspection
rules.explanation: Dogs, cats and ferrets need a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection completed by a licensed and accredited veterinarian within the 30 days before entry. No tests are required.

source.title: Indiana Board of Animal Health: Dogs, cats and ferrets entry requirements

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Every dog, cat or ferret that is 3 months of age or older must be vaccinated against rabies.

source.title: Indiana Board of Animal Health: Dogs, cats and ferrets entry requirements

rules.title: Certificate of Veterinary Inspection
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats entering Massachusetts must have a health certificate, which must indicate non-exposure to rabies.

source.title: Massachusetts Department of Agricultural Resources: Importing and exporting pets

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats over 6 months of age must be vaccinated against rabies not more than 12 months before importation.

requirement.ifNotMet: Massachusetts says an unvaccinated dog or cat must be vaccinated within 30 days of entry or at 6 months of age, whichever is later.

source.title: Massachusetts Department of Agricultural Resources: Importing and exporting pets

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs, cats and ferrets three months or older moved into Mississippi need proof of current rabies vaccination, as a certificate signed by a licensed veterinarian.

source.title: Mississippi Board of Animal Health: Regulations, chapter 12

rules.title: No certificate when accompanied by the owner
rules.explanation: Pets accompanied by their owner are not required to have a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection. One is needed for exhibition, change of ownership, adoption or pets travelling without their owner.

source.title: Mississippi Board of Animal Health: Regulations, chapter 12

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Small animals travelling with their owner need proof of current rabies vaccination.

source.title: Montana Department of Livestock: Import requirements

rules.title: No health certificate when travelling with your pet
rules.explanation: No health certificate is required for small animals travelling with their owner.

source.title: Montana Department of Livestock: Import requirements

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs, cats and ferrets over 12 weeks of age entering North Dakota for any length of time must be vaccinated against rabies, with a copy of the certificate.

source.title: North Dakota Department of Agriculture: Dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: Certificate only for stays over 30 days
rules.explanation: A Certificate of Veterinary Inspection is required for dogs, cats and ferrets entering North Dakota for longer than 30 days. APHIS Form 7001 is not accepted.

source.title: North Dakota Department of Agriculture: Dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: Certificate of Veterinary Inspection
rules.explanation: A Certificate of Veterinary Inspection issued by an accredited veterinarian is required for all dogs and cats, issued within 30 days before entering Oregon. A paper certificate also needs an import permit from the state; an approved electronic certificate does not.

source.title: Oregon Department of Agriculture: Import requirements

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats must be vaccinated against rabies, listed on the certificate. Puppies and kittens under 16 weeks of age are not required to be vaccinated.

source.title: Oregon Department of Agriculture: Import requirements

rules.title: Certificate of Veterinary Inspection
rules.explanation: Dogs, cats and ferrets entering South Carolina need a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection, valid for 30 days.

source.title: Clemson Livestock Poultry Health: Canine, feline and ferret import

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs, cats and ferrets need proof of rabies vaccination.

source.title: Clemson Livestock Poultry Health: Canine, feline and ferret import

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats 12 weeks of age or older must be vaccinated against rabies to be brought into Texas for any purpose. If the first vaccination was under 30 days before arrival, the pet should be confined for the rest of the 30 days.

source.title: Texas Department of State Health Services: Animal import and export requirements

rules.title: No state health certificate
rules.explanation: A Certificate of Veterinary Inspection is not required for dogs and cats entering Texas, although most airlines ask for a health certificate.

source.title: Texas Department of State Health Services: Animal import and export requirements

rules.title: No entry requirements for personal pets
rules.explanation: Virginia has no entry requirements for dogs and cats in personal ownership, and no permit is required. A certificate is needed only for sale, adoption, breeding or promotion.

source.title: Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: Animal admissions

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs, cats and ferrets entering Washington must be current on rabies vaccination. Animals less than ninety days of age do not require one. Family pets travelling with their owners need to carry the current rabies vaccination certificate.

source.title: Washington Administrative Code 16-54-170: Dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: No certificate for family pets travelling with you
rules.explanation: Family pets with current rabies certificates travelling with their owners, with no sale or change of ownership, are exempt from the certificate of veterinary inspection. Dogs owned by the same owner for more than a month are exempt from the heartworm test.

source.title: Washington Administrative Code 16-54-170: Dogs, cats and ferrets

rules.title: Certificate of Veterinary Inspection
rules.explanation: You must provide a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection when importing a household pet. It is good for 30 days from the date the animal is examined. No tests or import permits are required for household pets.

source.title: Wisconsin DATCP: Pet movement

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs and domestic cats 5 months and older need a current rabies vaccination given by a veterinarian.

source.title: Wisconsin DATCP: Pet movement

rules.title: Rabies vaccination (state rule)
rules.explanation: Dogs, cats and ferrets travelling as pets with no change of ownership need proof of current rabies vaccination if they are 3 months (12 weeks) of age or older. Younger animals need nothing.

rules.title: Certificate of Veterinary Inspection
rules.explanation: Dogs and cats need a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (valid for 30 days) if they are entering Tennessee for more than 15 days.

infoRoutes.summary: Only dogs and cats can be brought to India under the baggage rule. Birds, hamsters, rabbits, fish and other animals need a DGFT licence.
checklist: Apply for a DGFT licence (dgft.gov.in) before making travel plans
Ask AQCS at your port of entry what health conditions the licence will carry

source.title: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (India): FAQ

infoRoutes.summary: Ferrets from countries other than the United States need a CFIA import permit, applied for at least 30 days before travel. Ask the province for permission to keep a ferret.
checklist: Apply for a CFIA permit to import at least 30 days before travel
Contact the provincial authority about keeping ferrets

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

infoRoutes.summary: Pet rabbits from countries other than the United States need an import permit (apply at least 30 days ahead), a health certificate and quarantine in Canada at premises you arrange and CFIA approves.
checklist: Apply for a CFIA permit to import at least 30 days before travel
Arrange quarantine premises for CFIA approval
Send the full myxomatosis vaccination history if your rabbit was ever vaccinated

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

infoRoutes.summary: Most rodents can be imported to Canada without an import permit or health certificate. Prairie dogs, Gambian pouch rats and squirrels from most countries, and all rodents from Africa, are restricted.
checklist: Check your species is not restricted
Check with the Canadian Wildlife Service whether CITES applies

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

infoRoutes.summary: Most amphibians and reptiles can be imported without a permit or health certificate. Turtles and tortoises need an import permit applied for at least 30 days ahead, must have been in your personal possession and must travel with you.
checklist: For a turtle or tortoise, apply for a CFIA permit at least 30 days before travel
Contact the Canadian Wildlife Service about CITES

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

infoRoutes.summary: CFIA reviews each application to import a pet bird from countries other than the United States, and has separate requirements for pet aquatic animals. Check the CFIA tool for your exact case.
checklist: Use the CFIA tool for your species and origin country

source.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency: Bringing animals to Canada

infoRoutes.summary: Pet birds (five or fewer, not for resale, not poultry) need a USDA import permit, usually a health certificate, entry through a designated port (Los Angeles, Miami, New York) and in most cases a 30-day quarantine with testing.
checklist: Apply for the USDA import permit at least 7 business days before shipping (valid 30 days)
Book the 30-day federal quarantine
Ask the state veterinarian whether a state quarantine also applies

source.title: USDA APHIS: Bring a pet bird into the United States

infoRoutes.summary: USDA has no animal health requirements for pet ferrets, rabbits, rodents or amphibians entering the United States. CDC prohibits rodents of African origin, and not every state allows ferrets.
checklist: Check your destination state allows the species
Check the animal is not an African-origin rodent

source.title: USDA APHIS: Bring a pet from another country into the United States

infoRoutes.summary: USDA prohibits leopard tortoises, African spurred tortoises and Bell's hingeback tortoises; otherwise it has no health requirements for pet reptiles. CDC allows up to six small turtles for non-commercial purposes.
checklist: Check your species is not prohibited
Check your destination state's rules

source.title: USDA APHIS: Bring a pet reptile into the United States

infoRoutes.summary: Hawaii prohibits many animals from entry or private possession, for example hamsters, gerbils, snakes, geckos, bearded dragons, alligators, snapping turtles, hermit crabs, piranhas, lories, monk parakeets and toucans.
checklist: Check the Plant Quarantine list for your species
Call Hawaii Plant Quarantine on (808) 832-0566 before booking

source.title: Hawaii Plant Quarantine: Animal guidelines

infoRoutes.summary: Pet birds can come to Ireland from the EU and listed European territories with an owner declaration and advance notice. Poultry-type species (chickens, turkeys, guinea fowl, ducks, geese, quails, pigeons, partridges, ratites) follow different rules.
checklist: Fill in the Owner Declaration Pet Birds EU form and carry it with you
Email the Form of Advance Notice of Importation of Pet Birds to livetrade@agriculture.gov.ie at least 24 hours before arrival
Ask the National Parks and Wildlife Service (cites@housing.gov.ie) whether a CITES licence is needed
Carry original paperwork, not copies
Travel with your bird, or within 5 days of it

source.title: DAFM Pet Travel Portal: Birds

infoRoutes.summary: Pet rabbits and rodents can come to Ireland from the EU and listed European territories with an owner declaration sent in advance.
checklist: Fill in the Owner Declaration (pet rodent or rabbit from an EU country) and email it to livetrade@agriculture.gov.ie at least one working day before arrival
Check your pet meets the health requirements in the declaration
Ask the National Parks and Wildlife Service (cites@housing.gov.ie) whether a CITES licence is needed
Travel with your pet, or within 5 days of it

source.title: DAFM Pet Travel Portal: Rabbits and rodents

infoRoutes.summary: Ireland's rules for this kind of pet depend on the species and the country you travel from. Select the species and country on the official portal to see what applies.
checklist: Look up your species and origin country on the DAFM Pet Travel Portal
Ask the National Parks and Wildlife Service whether a CITES licence is needed

source.title: DAFM Pet Travel Portal
